key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen perovskite samples from short accelerated-aging measurements.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster, more explainable way to screen perovskite stability, potentially reducing experimental test time for solar-cell materials development.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to encode degradation-relevant descriptors.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for samples not seen during training.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on a diverse dataset spanning different crystallinities and compositions and was reported to generalize across material groups while outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the accelerated-aging dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
